title: Plugin architecture
idea: A pluggable design is a small, stable core that exposes extension points, so new features arrive as separate modules the core never names.
points: The core defines a contract: what a plugin must provide and when it runs.
Plugins register with the core through hooks; the core calls them without knowing them.
Unlike c04-t08's one extension point, a host offers many hooks; config picks modules.
Each plugin is its own module exporting one object; the host keeps `#hooks` private.

edges.label: chooses plugins
edges.caption: Config lists which plugins to load and their order. The core's source never changes.

edges.label: implements
edges.caption: Every plugin meets one contract: a `name` and a `setup(host)` function.

edges.label: implements
edges.caption: A new plugin is a new module. Nothing else is edited.

edges.label: setup(host)
edges.caption: `use()` calls `setup`, and the plugin registers a handler with `on('price', …)`.

edges.label: run hook
edges.caption: Core code fires the hook. Each registered handler runs in order, passing the value along.

walk.text: The contract, written as a JSDoc interface: a name and a `setup` function.
`use` rejects anything that breaks the contract, then lets the plugin register itself.
`on` is the extension point: plugins attach handlers to a named hook.
`run` passes a value through every handler, in registration order.
Each plugin is a plain object; it knows the host, not the other plugins.
With or without plugins, the core runs. Plugins add behaviour, not requirements.

code.title: Loading by config
code.caption: Same contract as before; a config object now picks the plugins and their order.

walk.text: Each plugin meets the same contract: a `name` and a `setup` that calls `on`.
This host offers only `on`, the one extension point plugins need.
Config picks the plugins and their order; unknown names fail at load time.
One core, two configs, two different pipelines.
A typo in the config fails loudly with a clear message.

pitfalls: Do not let plugins import each other; share data only through the host's hooks.
Validate each plugin against the contract at load time, not on first use.
Document hook order when handlers transform values; order changes results.

quiz.q: Using the `Host` from the example, what does this print?
quiz.why: Handlers run in registration order: `vat` makes 100 into 120, then `tenOff` subtracts 10, giving 110.

takeaway: Keep the core small and stable; let features plug in through contracts.
